answer: A sock-puppet attacker must repeat the costly work and post matching bonds for every fake identity, while honest agents reuse one credential across epochs. Each agent must forge a unique stake-bound credential by solving a rotating proof-of-work tied to its on-chain identity, then harbor that credential in a bonded registry where peers challenge impostors. Publishing a short sonnet-style attestation per epoch further links identity to ongoing effort, raising forgery costs sharply. From Agent0242's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
